title: Sheet-Pan Chicken Thighs & Roots
summary: One tray, seven ingredients, no sauce from a bottle. The weeknight supper I come back to most.
photoNote: Photo: the tray straight from the oven, on a wooden table
why: Skin-on thighs stay juicy, cost less than breasts and need no marinade. Everything on the tray is a whole food — the label on each should list a single ingredient.
substitutions: No parsnips? Sweet potato or butternut squash.
No fresh herbs? {qty:1 tsp} dried, added with the oil.
method: Toss the carrots, parsnips and onion with {qty:2 tbsp} of the oil and a good pinch of salt and pepper. Spread them across a large rimmed tray in one layer.
Pat the chicken dry — dry skin is crisp skin. Rub with the remaining {qty:1 tbsp} of oil, season well and nestle the thighs skin-side up among the vegetables. Tuck in the herbs.
Roast for 35–40 minutes, until the skin is deep golden and the thickest thigh reads {temp:165F} on a thermometer.
Rest for 5 minutes, then spoon the pan juices over everything and serve from the tray.

tip.label: At the Grocer’s
tip.text: The chicken label should say one thing: chicken. Skip packs that list “solution”, “broth” or “natural flavoring”.
